correctness.rationale: The four dot products give max(cos θ,a sin θ)+max(cos θ,b sin θ) on the uniform reduced quadrant. The two switches order as p≤q; intersecting the applicable cosine and sine sublevel sets with their respective intervals gives exactly the three CDF terms, including empty intervals and thresholds at branch maxima. The middle sine is concave, so minima lie at switches, and its derivative vanishes strictly inside exactly when 2p<π/2<p+q, equivalent to b>1 and ab<1. The outer endpoints are strict one-sided maxima; at a boundary equality the middle junction itself is not a third maximum. Each inverse branch there or at the interior peak contributes (2/π)/sqrt(M²−t²); multiplicities two, one, and zero give the interior, boundary, and empty-branch coefficients. Integrating each max(cos θ,k sin θ) on the quadrant independently gives sqrt(1+k²), verifying the mean. The example's peak levels round to 1.9171592980, 1.9508234187 and 2, and its minimum to 1.7172502208. The law is in the stated normalized length units: for original horizontal-diagonal half-length L, use F(t/L). The frozen numerical checker was inspected, not executed; the exact argument covers all shapes and the numerical checks do not establish it.
